title: GitLab Dedicated: A go-live guide
summary:
GitLab Dedicated is a single-tenant SaaS solution that is fully isolated, deployed in your preferred AWS cloud region, and hosted and maintained by GitLab. GitLab Dedicated and compliance covers why regulated organizations choose a single-tenant instance operated by GitLab, and serves as a starting point for evaluation. In this article, you'll learn what to do after you sign on to GitLab Dedicated, including understanding which responsibilities GitLab takes on and which remain with your teams, as well as what controls each team needs to put in place.

Teams arriving from any self-managed source-control or CI/CD platform bring an operating model built around upgrade runbooks, pre-flight checks, staging environments, and rollback plans. title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
summary:
AWS has raised the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018. AWS's post lists the costs: twice the concurrency at the same request rate, three-hour SQS visibility timeouts, and Kafka mappings that must be recreated. Practitioners welcome it and ask what belongs elsewhere.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
summary:
Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) after ten years of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in dependency cooldown setting. Some critics note the allocator design still lacks inline storage support.

By Daniel Curtis
